title: Dear Teacher
author: Michel Delving
summary: Michel Delving's 'Dear Teacher' is a satirical letter from the perspective of a disengaged student, expressing sarcastic 'gratitude' to teachers for everything corporate media culture and social media would prefer schools not provide: recognizing learning differences, delivering honest sex education, modeling healthy personal boundaries, teaching the value of failure and persistence, and celebrating inherent student worth. By inverting the praise--'thanks for nothing!'--the piece makes visible all that teachers do that no algorithm, platform, or advertiser will ever provide. The satirical student voice is fully immersed in influencer culture, crypto, content metrics, and entertainment--and genuinely cannot see why these are insufficient. The piece's sharpest moment identifies the deepest failure of markets as child-rearing environments: the market will never tell a child they have inherent value and dignity. The piece functions as a quietly devastating defense of the teacher's countercultural role.
points: * The 'thanks for nothing' satirical structure makes visible all that teachers provide that no corporate entity, social platform, or algorithm will: disability advocacy, honest sex education, healthy boundaries, accountability grading. * The satirical student voice is recognizable: fully fluent in influencer culture, crypto, content metrics, and instant entertainment--and genuinely unable to see why these are insufficient substitutes for what teachers offer. * The piece's sharpest implication: the market will not tell a child they have inherent dignity and value--but a teacher will, and does. * Healthy boundaries, privacy protection, and honest accountability (failing students who don't meet standards) are precisely the things that corporate culture and social media actively undermine. * The ironic inversion forces the reader to name aloud everything teachers actually do--and recognize how much of it has no market substitute.
quotes: Thanks for pushing for my individual learning challenges to be recognized, diagnosed, and supported. It really sucks when people try harder to understand me and the very unique way in which my brain operates.
You made it clear to me that my uniqueness is a feature and not a bug.
Thanks for being the only person in the world to try to teach me sexual education in a healthy way. Don't you know that's what the internet's for?
Why would I ever need to learn that sometimes in life you fail, and you have to reevaluate your approach and pick the pieces back up and try again. And again. And again.
